tasks.statement: `boltons.setutils.IndexedSet.update()` is documented to accept one or more iterables, but calling it with several fails: `IndexedSet([1]).update([2], [3])` raises `TypeError`, and passing tuples or iterators adds the argument objects themselves as members. Expected: `s = IndexedSet([1]); s.update([2, 1, 3], [], [3, 4, 2])` returns None and leaves `list(s) == [1, 2, 3, 4]` for list, tuple, and one-shot iterator arguments; tuple-valued elements stay elements (`IndexedSet().update([(1, 2)], [(3, 4), (1, 2)])` gives `[(1, 2), (3, 4)]`).

`boltons.strutils.iter_splitlines()` corrupts ordinary text containing a space followed by 28 or 29: `list(iter_splitlines('February 28, 2026'))` returns `['February', ', 2026']`. `indent()` inherits the corruption. It should split on the Unicode line separator U+2028 and paragraph separator U+2029 (e.g. `' first second '` -> `['', 'first', 'second', '']`), leave text like 'February 28, or February 29 in a leap year' as one line, and `indent('February 28 February 29 March 1
March 2', '  ')` should return `'  February 28
  February 29
  March 1
  March 2'`.

`more_itertools.constrained_batches(['a', 'b', 'c'], 10, max_count=0)` yields all three items in one batch, and negative `max_count` values are silently ignored. A supplied `max_count` of zero or less should raise `ValueError` with a message containing 'maximum count must be greater than zero', raised before any input is consumed (also for empty input). `max_count=None` still means no limit, and `max_count=1` yields one-item batches.

`more_itertools.one()` and `only()` ignore a custom `too_long` / `too_short` exception instance whose truth value is False (an exception class defining `__bool__` returning False) and raise the default `ValueError` instead. The supplied exception should always be raised. Also, when a custom `too_long` exception is supplied, the default error message (which calls `repr()` on the first items) must not be built, so items whose `__repr__` raises do not interfere.

`packaging.metadata` treats the `charset` parameter of `Description-Content-Type` as case-sensitive. `Metadata.from_email()` with `Description-Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8` (Metadata-Version 2.6) does not produce `meta.description_content_type == 'text/plain; charset=utf-8'`, and validation rejects `text/plain; charset=utf-8` and `text/plain; charset=Utf-8` even though they name UTF-8. Charset values that resolve to UTF-8 should be accepted case-insensitively; other charsets such as ascii remain invalid.

Assigning an array of tables over a dotted key swallows the following sibling on round-trip:
```python
import tomlkit
doc = tomlkit.parse('a.b = 1\nc.d = 2\n')
aot = tomlkit.aot()
t = tomlkit.table(); t['x'] = 9
aot.append(t)
doc['a'] = aot
print(tomlkit.dumps(doc))
```
prints `[[a]]\nx = 9\nc.d = 2\n`, so `c.d` is captured by `[[a]]` and the top-level `c` is lost when reparsed. Expected output: `'c.d = 2\n\n[[a]]\nx = 9\n'`, which reparses to `{'c': {'d': 2}, 'a': [{'x': 9}]}`.

`tomlkit.string(value, multiline=True)` loses a leading newline on round-trip. For `s = tomlkit.string('
foo', multiline=True)`, `str(s)` is `'
foo'`, but parsing `f'k = {s.as_string()}
'` gives `'foo'`. A multiline string (basic or literal) whose value starts with `
` or `
` must reparse to exactly the original value; values that do not start with a newline must render as before.

tasks.statement: `pyparsing_common.as_datetime` produces the wrong microseconds for fractional seconds: `ppc.iso8601_datetime().add_parse_action(ppc.as_datetime).parse_string('1997-07-16T19:20:30.45')[0]` is `datetime(1997, 7, 16, 19, 20, 30, 449)` but should be `datetime(1997, 7, 16, 19, 20, 30, 450000)`, matching `convert_to_datetime` and `datetime.fromisoformat`.

Growing an existing entry in a size-bounded cache evicts an unrelated entry even when the result fits: with `c = cachetools.LRUCache(maxsize=10, getsizeof=lambda v: v)`, doing `c[3] = 3; c[4] = 4; c[4] = 7` leaves only key 4, although 3 + 7 == 10 fits. Expected: both keys remain and `currsize == 10`. Replacing with the same size or a smaller size must also keep both entries with the correct `currsize`. This applies to every cache class in the package.

`humanize.naturalsize()` shows a mantissa equal to the base instead of moving to the next unit when rounding crosses a unit boundary: `naturalsize(999999)` returns `'1000.0 kB'` (expected `'1.0 MB'`), `naturalsize(999999999)` -> expected `'1.0 GB'`, `naturalsize(999999999999)` -> `'1.0 TB'`, `naturalsize(1024**2 - 1, binary=True)` -> `'1.0 MiB'`, `naturalsize(1024**3 - 1, binary=True)` -> `'1.0 GiB'`, and `naturalsize(1024**2 - 1, gnu=True)` -> `'1.0M'`. Values at the largest suffix are unaffected.

`get_real_name()` returns the wrong component for names with more than two dotted parts: `sqlparse.parse('db.schema.tbl.col')[0].tokens[0].get_real_name()` returns `'schema'` but should return `'col'` (and `get_name()` should also return `'col'`), while `get_parent_name()` remains `'db'`. For `x.y.z AS w` the real name should be `'z'` with alias `'w'`; `mydb.sch.func(1)` should give `'func'`. Two-part names such as `a.b` -> `'b'` already work.

`marshmallow.validate.URL()` rejects an absolute URL with a fragment right after the host: `validate.URL()('http://example.org#fragment')` raises `ValidationError: Not a valid URL.`, while `http://example.org/#fragment` passes. `http://example.org#fragment` and `http://user@example.com#fragment` should be valid, and a bare same-document reference `#frag` should be valid when relative URLs are allowed (`relative=True`, and `relative=True, absolute=False`).

Rendering markdown that ends on a blockquote marker while a table is open inside the quote crashes with `IndexError: string index out of range`:
```python
from markdown_it import MarkdownIt
MarkdownIt().enable('table').render('> | a | b |\n> |---|---|\n>')
MarkdownIt('commonmark', {'html': False}).enable('table').render('> | a | b |\n> |---|---|\n>')
```
Both calls should render without raising.

`click._utils.Sentinel` members (such as `click._utils.UNSET`) do not survive `copy.copy`, `copy.deepcopy`, or `pickle` round-trips: the result is not the same singleton member (or the operation fails). Every duplication of a member should return the identical member object. As a consequence, `copy.copy`/`copy.deepcopy`/pickling of `click.Option(['--name'])`, whose `default` is `UNSET`, should give an option whose `default is UNSET` and `name == 'name'`.
